label: <DEL> and last ~3 copy steps of length-9 sequences (sparse, token-gated)
explanation: Never fires during the original phase. All activity is at the <DEL> step (19% of mass) or in the copy phase (81%), and almost only for long sequences (L=9 holds 83% of mass, L=8 15%, nothing for L<=5). Within a sequence it fires at <DEL> (output orig 0) and on the final copy steps (recall_idx 6-8; rate climbs to 20% at t=17); the middle copy steps are silent. This position window covers 81% of activation mass but only about 15% of those steps fire. Which ones fire depends on token content: input tokens 0, f, 2, n, h raise the rate (in_tok 0 lift 4.9x), and sequences with more digits fire more often (n_digits 6 gives 10x lift). Adding a token-set filter raises precision to about 0.5 but cuts mass recall to about 0.4, and no simple token rule explains the content dependence. The largest activations are at <DEL> when the sequence opens with f/0/z followed by f f.
